title: How many seconds is fifteen million years?
description: Fifteen million years is changed into seconds using powers of ten. Then the time to count every star of the universe, and the time to drink all the drops of water on Earth, are found. Keeko doubts that only the unit changes.
teaching_notes: One idea: work on the numbers in front and the powers of ten separately, then put them together. Watch for students who change the unit but keep the same number, as if a year were one second.

source: Convert 15 million years to seconds; time to count 2 × 10 to the power 23 stars at one per second; time to drink 2 × 10 to the power 25 drops at 200 ml every 10 seconds
video_script.why: Huge times are found by working on the numbers in front and the powers of ten separately: multiply the numbers and add the powers, or divide the numbers and subtract the powers.
video_script.substitution: Write each quantity with one digit before the point and a power of ten, then multiply or divide the numbers in front and add or subtract the powers.
video_script.anchor: fifteen million years in seconds, counting every star, and drinking every drop of water
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko changes only the unit and keeps the number, so fifteen million years becomes fifteen million seconds. But one year alone is about 3.15 × 10 to the power 7 seconds, so the seconds are about 4.7 × 10 to the power 14.
video_script.payoff_line: Work on the numbers in front and the powers of ten separately

final_answer.value: about 4.7 × 10 to the power 14 seconds; 2 × 10 to the power 23 seconds; 6.25 × 10 to the power 22 seconds
final_answer.spoken: Fifteen million years is about four point seven times ten to the power fourteen seconds. Counting takes two times ten to the power twenty three seconds. Drinking takes six point two five times ten to the power twenty two seconds.

maths_rules: counting at one per second takes 2 × 10²³ seconds
2 × 10²⁵ drops ÷ 16 = 1.25 × 10²⁴ ml; ÷ 200 ml = 6.25 × 10²¹ glasses; × 10 seconds = 6.25 × 10²² seconds
the slip: keeping 15 million and changing only the unit gives 15 million seconds, which is far too small
video_script.design: The three quantities appear as three lines on the working area. Each line builds the numbers in front first, then the powers of ten, in two colours.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='yrs'/>Change fifteen million years into seconds.
<bookmark mark='cnt'/>Then count every star of the universe, one star each second. There are two times ten to the power twenty three of them.
<bookmark mark='drink'/>Next, drink two times ten to the power twenty five drops of water.
<bookmark mark='rate'/>Sixteen drops make one millilitre, and you drink two hundred millilitres every ten seconds. How long would it take?

<bookmark mark='front'/>Multiply the numbers in front, two times three is six.
<bookmark mark='pow'/>Add the powers, three plus two is five. That is six times ten to the power five.

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, the years. Fifteen million is one point five times ten to the power seven.
<bookmark mark='front1'/>Multiply the numbers in front, one point five times three point one five. That is four point seven two five.
<bookmark mark='pw1'/>Add the powers, seven plus seven is fourteen.

beats.on_screen: one star each second: the seconds match the count, 2 × 10²³ seconds

marks.same: the seconds match the count, 2 × 10²³ seconds, is written below it

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, the counting. Each count takes one second.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The seconds match the count, two times ten to the power twenty three.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, the water. Sixteen drops make one millilitre, so divide the drops by sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ml'/>That is one point two five times ten to the power twenty four millilitres.

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, the glasses. Each holds two hundred millilitres, so divide the millilitres by two hundred.
<bookmark mark='gl'/>That gives six point two five times ten to the power twenty one glasses.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Each glass takes ten seconds, so multiply by ten.
